questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The reason why I wanted to go on exchange is because I wanted to see how it is studying and living in another country. The reason why I specifically chose Hong Kong is because I have relatives there and wanted to see how their daily life is.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I got all information on email, so it was easy to find the information I needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had to quarantine when I arrived, so we were send there by bus directly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Undergraduate exchange students were guaranteed housing on campus, so they had several options - both with and without meal plans. I, as a postgraduate, was not guaranteed housing on campus, but was lucky that I got it.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: At the dorm I stayed at, we had shared bathrooms and a shared kitchen, but we had to buy our own equipments.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's much cheaper than finding your own housing off campus, but don't expect luxury.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Because I am a master's student I had to apply as a postgraduate, even though I only had undergraduate courses at the university. I was just lucky that I got housing on campus, since only undergraduate exchange students were guaranteed housing on campus. UCPH should allow students to apply as undergraduates, if they allow us to take undergraduate courses. I also talked to other exchange master's students and a lot of them told me that their university recommended them to apply as undergraduates, because of the benefits.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't remember all the details, but one thing I remember is that we had to send a lot of physical documents through post, which was a little stressful. It would have been easier if we could send it through e-mail.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university has a very nice student advisor for exchange students, so I could contact her with all my questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I found out that I couldn't register for all the courses I wanted from my course pre approval, because they were not available for exchange students. But I found some other courses that I wanted to register for and I got those, but I heard it was a little stressful for others, because they wanted some "popular" courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the instructions and it will be fine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level of the courses were mostly the same as at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The lectures were mostly the same style as at UCHP, but the teaching classes were very different from UCPH's. A lot of students didn't show up. But I think it's because the teaching assistant is just solving problems without really interacting with the students and also because the teaching classes were recorded.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON3460 - Development Economics
ECON3480 - Industrial Organization
ECON3570 - Information Technology and Economics
ECON4810 - Selected Topics in Economics I: Introduction to Machine Learning Methods in Economics
STAT4001 - Data Mining and Statistical Learning

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ECON4810 - Selected Topics in Economics I: Introduction to Machine Learning Methods in Economics and STAT4001 - Data Mining and Statistical Learning. Good lecturers and interesting.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food from the supermarket was more expensive than expected, but it was not that expensive eating out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had different events for exchange students. The different dorms also had events. All in all, there was a lot of events happening all the time.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Attend all the free activities i-House provide. They were educational and you got to know other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit the different islands and just explore the city!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. I didn't find it difficult at all.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I think the easiest way is to talk to the local students in class

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I don't know

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don't be afraid of not getting any friends.
2. Try to be openminded
3. Do it!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't think so

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Everything

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Saying goodbye to the people I met there

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
